text_fidelity_a:
VIOFO Dash Cam Front and Rear 2K 1440P 60fps +1080P 30fps Dual Dash Camera with Wi-Fi GPS, Emergency Recording, Motion Detection, 24h Parking Mode, Super Capacitor (A129 Plus Duo) This is a terrific kit, complete with everything to get you started... Some important notes...

1.) If you already have a camera in place that uses mini usb, then half the battle is already won. Most of these cameras use mini usbs.

2.) The Viofo has a capacitor battery, which is what you want, especially if you live in the hot areas. They are not prone to ballooning like lithium batteries.

3.) Instructions say to slide the camera onto a mounting plate, which has an adhesive backing, you then remove the adhesive cover and stick entire unit on the glass. But it comes to you preinstalled, at least mind was. All you have to do is peel the adhesive cover and stick the unit onto your glass. Out of curiosity, I tried to remove the plate, but I couldn't, it is very tight. So if you stick the unit to your window, taking it down for whatever reason will be a pain. I don't see how you can dismount the camera and leave the plate on the window. You would have to take the plate with you, which means ripping the adhesive from the glass.

So here's my tip... I'd like to be able to remove the camera, fiddle with it, change settings, etc. without hassle. Or perhaps, even dismount and hide my camera in the glove compartment when I need to. If you install it the way they tell you to, you will never take this camera down. My solution for this is using strong round earth magnets. I installed a round earth magnet on the back of the unit. This is easy, since it already has an adhesive back, just remove the cover and stick a magnet on it. Then I install another one directly onto the glass. These neodymium magnets are very strong and the hold is absolutely solid. This is how I install dashcams for myself and family. I have not installed the rearview, but I'll be using the same method. This is another review using the same method: https://www.amazon.com/gp/customer-reviews/RETFFEWXHSOJ6/ref=cm_cr_getr_d_rvw_ttl?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B088B6372Z

This is a 5-Star kit!
text_fidelity_b: VIOFO Dash Cam Front and Rear 2K 1440P 60fps +1080P 30fps Dual Dash Camera with Wi-Fi GPS, Emergency Recording, Motion Detection, 24h Parking Mode, Super Capacitor (A129 Plus Duo)

month to send back a refurb, rather than the one my son sent in with his music on it.

My daughter's lasted a little longer, but does freeze up often.

She had purchased four pairs of various headphones trying to get the sound to stop
cutting out, thinking it was the headphone's problem. Nope - turns out, it is the
player. Don't know what is wrong, but one of the stereo sides cuts in and out endlessly.

She'll be shopping for a new one, but it won't be this model anymore.
They are just too cheaply made to last. The technology has been around for a long time now,
and it shouldn't be that hard to make a decent, affordable player.
However, it seems like it might just be too hard for Sansa.

Sunhans Sh-2500 2500mw Wireless Signal Repeater 33dbm Wifi Signal Booster 2.5w Since there are detailed specs in the product description I will not repeat them here. Instead I'll use my personal experience with this kit to explain why I rated it five stars.

I used the review sample I received to extend the range of my ancient [[ASIN:B000BTL0OA Linksys WRT54GL Wireless-G Broadband Router]] (which is still working as well as when I purchased it ten years ago!) I removed one antenna from the Linksys, used a [[ASIN:B005IKGTXY Bluecell SMA female to TNC male Coaxial Adapter/Converter]] to adapt the included cable to the antenna connector, plugged it into the power supply and checked my home dead spot.

My dead spot is the master bedroom and my phone is always complaining about 'unstable WiFi connections' when I am in the room. I used an app called [[ASIN:B004EBZX6W Wi-Fi Analyzer]] to perform the before and after tests.

Before I installed this booster kit I was getting a strong reading of -45 dBm near the router and an absymal -80 dBm in the dead room. After installing this kit the signal boosted to -55 dBm in the bedroom, so this booster kit works as advertised.

It's practically worth its weight in gold if you do have dead areas in your WiFi coverage. Based on my experience and how easy and fast this is to install I rate this as a five star product.

Because I have the waterproof case for the 110, I used it whenever I was shooting in wet areas and also for underwater shots. I used the SX500 in dry locations. In some instances, I was able to take comparable shots with both cameras and the difference was really striking. Let me preface this by saying that I'm NOT a photographer. I'm just someone who likes to take a lot of pictures. I like them to come out well, but I know virtually nothing about photography beyond what I've learned through trial and error.

I found the low-light shots taken with the SX500 to be FAR superior than those taken with the Elph. Yes, it's difficult to capture a moving subject in low light. This isn't and expensive, professional camera. I'm very pleased with the results considering the price I paid.

The biggest selling feature was the zoom lens. I was absolutely AMAZED how clear shots taken from VERY far away came out. I took this camera to Opening Day, to see the Red Sox players get their World Series rings. We didn't have the best of seats, so I had to really max out the zoom lens. I was certain the photos would be blurry. It's difficult to hold a camera really still, extremely zoomed in, while standing in a crowd. The photos were OUTSTANDING. I mean really...outstanding!

I'm extremely pleased with this purchase. The camera is small and easy to carry with the strap around my neck. When I want something I can slip in my pocket, I opt for the Elph.

I would classify this as a bridge camera. It's NOT as easy to carry around as a pocket-sized digital, but it's also not as cumbersome to carry around as a more professional model. It's EASY to use...even for novices like me! And it takes great photos. I'm sure as I have more trial-and-error lessons under my belt, my shots will be even better.

Netgear Unite AC770S | Mobile Wifi Hotspot 4G LTE | Up to 300Mbps Download Speed | Connect Up to 10 Devices | Create A WLAN Anywhere | 2 MIMO TS-9 external antenna connectors | GSM Unlocked - Black I'll update if there's a problem once I receive my FREE SIM card with FREE Express Mail from AT&T. The unit comes charged, and everything worked perfectly, connected to my laptop, WiFi name & password printed on sticker. Very, very nice, compact, well-designed device. Easy connection, easy info once I learned to use the built-in electronic screen and "Info". The "ICCID" number is the SIM number, it's under "Info" with the IMEA number in the electronic screen (AT&T will need both numbers for activation). The IMEA is also listed beneath battery. Slide two little metal sliders on side to remove back cover to remove battery. But you don't have to, it's in the electronic screen "Info" :)

Persons much more mechanically inclined than I will see that the door to the SIM card is on the side edge, not in the back or under the battery. I would have ruined the device trying to dig out the back compartment if my husband hadn't stopped me. He needed tweezers to get out the SIM card regardless.

This is a great, mobile, easy HotSpot device that works just like any Wi-Fi on any device with a great connection. Mobile supposedly for 10 hours, less than hour recharge.

There's only one caveat: AT&T will tell you the pre-installed SIM card it comes with, sealed in new packaging, is INVALID. AT&T will give you a good one for FREE. You simply have to replace it, or if you're like me, get someone that can. :) That simple, and you're ready for set-up. *NOTE*: Both the pre-installed SIM card *AND* the SIM card being sold by a separate seller on Amazon that is suggested as being a good companion purchase with this device are INVALID. This according to AT&T themselves. They will send you a new, free one you can use; tell them what device you have and setup a data plan.

All you need then is to add a Data plan. This device, according to AT&T, *only* works with a postpaid plan ($50.00/month for 5 G's minimum), however there's no contract. There is a credit check. It will not work with prepaid, it will not work with a lesser plan, no matter what the packaging or Amazon description says. I just spent like 20 minutes on the phone with a very helpful, patient, and knowledgeable AT&T customer service representative who also consulted another department for verification.

The one exception is if you already have an AT&T cellphone plan (I do), you can "share" your data package you already have for only $20/month. So that's what I did. It still is postpaid, and there still is no contract on that part of the plan with your new HotSpot device. You'll be given a new number that's only for the HotSpot without a cellphone (Voice) plan component.

I'm really glad I bought this great device, I was a little apprehensive because I'm not techie and I've never tried a mobile HotSpot device before. To make it simple, get AT&T to install (instore) or send you a new SIM card that they say works with this device, and then you can set up the device (supposedly) online with ease. You have to add a data plan for it. I'll update if there's a problem, but the connection to my laptop worked seamlessly and looking through the device hardware and software on the electronic screen, it's designed beautifully and is a definite winner! :) :)

ps. Oh!, and it DOES receive 4G out of the box! :) Shows right in the screen corner like a Cellphone would with the bars.
text_fidelity_b: Netgear Unite AC770S | Mobile Wifi Hotspot 4G LTE | Up to 300Mbps Download Speed | Connect Up to 10 Devices | Create A WLAN Anywhere | 2 MIMO TS-9 external antenna connectors | GSM Unlocked - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Toshiba N300 6TB NAS 3.5-Inch Internal Hard Drive - CMR SATA 6 GB/s 7200 RPM 128 MB Cache - HDWN160XZSTA A NAS is a great way to add storage for the whole network where everything can be reached from any system connected. It is not as simple as a USB mass storage device like a thumb drive, of course, but it addresses a completely different issue. So far, this drive has proven to be a good one, though its reliability remains to be demonstrated over the long haul.

I have the 8TB drive, and it is great for dumping huge numbers of videos, music, documents and other media needed across a small network. It is fairly fast too, so streaming video from the NAS to any given device on the network is reasonably smooth as long as the network can handle the bandwidth (keep this detail in mind if you are wanting to stream video over a slower wireless network - the lag isn’t necessarily the drive’s fault). The drive is very quiet, though not silent, and so far seems to stay acceptably cool.

I did learn that it does not work all that well in a USB drive enclosure right out of the packaging. I have an enclosure that is capable of handling drives up to 8TB so I decided to try an experiment with the drive when it first arrived. I put it in the enclosure and connected it to my Windows 10 laptop. The system saw the device, and it even saw the drive and recognized the model and serial number, but it was unable to access the drive or even format it. I had more success with my Linux system which recognized the drive and was able to access the partition table and display drive parameters. I did not repartition the drive or create a file system for my experiment though I believe it would have worked.

Time will tell if this drive will be reliable over the long haul. Based on my experience so far, it has worked out well and I have had no issues. It’s the largest drive I have worked with and can handle a LOT of data. If you need wide open spaces for your network storage solution (or you are willing to fiddle with it to get it working as a USB solution) this is a good choice.
text_fidelity_b: Toshiba N300 6TB NAS 3.5-Inch Internal Hard Drive - CMR SATA 6 GB/s 7200 RPM 128 MB Cache - HDWN160XZSTA

I chose this watch because of the blood pressure (bp) monitor, I have high blood pressure and I take medication to keep it normal. Throughout the day I repeated the test and the watch was constantly reading that my blood pressure was high, even after I had taken my medication and I know the readings should have changed.  I will have to get with my doctor/nurse and have them do a manual test and see if the watch is showing the same results.  If the watch bp monitor is not accurate, I have not been able to find any way to recalibrate the watch to input the correct bp reading.  That is the only problem I have with this watch.  I like all the features the watch has along with the phone app too.  It doesn't take long to learn all the functions of the watch as well as the app.  If you have high blood pressure, I wouldn't rely on just the watch to monitor your blood pressure because I don't believe it is accurate enough.  Maybe in time there will be an upgrade in the software to fix that. Other than that it is a great sport watch and I am happy with it overall.
text_fidelity_b: Pard Young Men Smart Watch, Cool Fitness Tracker with Heart Rate Blood Pressure SpO2 Monitor, White

ASUS Transformer Infinity TF700T Mobile Docking - Champagne I bought this at the same time I bought an Infinity TF700. I'm glad I did. I find screen touchpad typing difficult and I have pretty big hands. The keys on this are quite nice. Very good positive feel and comparable to most laptop keyboards. Complete set of Android function keys that cover just about everything. No need to be touching the screen. I wish the mouse pad was just a bit better. It's more than functional I guess. The unit connects and disconnects nicely and has a lock lever which latches automatically. You can open it to about a 140 degree angle which makes getting a comforatble viewing angle possible in virtually any situation. If feels quite solid with no free play. Nice snug fit.

Folded closed with the TF700 attached it's about 3/4 inch thick at the most and makes a nice sleek package. Connected together the two weigh right at 2.5 lbs.

The current price seems a bit high compared to other tablet's docking ports, but the keyboard is superior and the other features are quite nice. It's a worthwhile addition. I'd give it 5 stars if it were about $50 cheaper.

text_fidelity_a:
Bone Conduction Headphones with Noise Cancelling MIC for Clear Calls, IPX6 Waterproof Open-Ear Bluetooth Wireless Headset for Calling, Running, Bicycling, Hiking (Green) Bone conduction headphones have become quite popular and because of this, there are many to choose from. This specific model is quite minimalist. A thin metal frame with the vibration units and electronics hanging off it.

In terms of comfort, there is no adjustability to the metal frame so it may take some getting used to because the frame may feel like they are too big or too small depending on your head size. For me it felt a little bit loose but I came to realize that it actually stayed where you place it and it really wasn't a problem.

For sound quality, this bone conduction headphone will never match a nice pair of over-ear headphones but that really isn't what it's for. By leaving the ears open, one is still able to stay aware of the surroundings, making it great for cycling and jogging where hearing the traffic is essential for safety reasons.

A pair of earplugs are included with this product and with one or both in, one can really appreciate the difference between regular headphones and bone conduction. You can still hear the music (or in my case, audiobook) through the earplugs because of the bone vibration but all outside sound is cut off. This means that you'd be able to listen to music over the sound of a loud machine.

I have tried a few different pairs of bone conduction headphones and these are the ones that I have stuck with so far. The buttons maybe be somewhat limited (just two buttons that control volume and power), but they are easily reachable and not hard to press and the IPX6 means it's water resistant against rain and sweat.
text_fidelity_b: Bone Conduction Headphones with Noise Cancelling MIC for Clear Calls, IPX6 Waterproof Open-Ear Bluetooth Wireless Headset for Calling, Running, Bicycling, Hiking (Green)

text_fidelity_a:
Wacom Intuos Intuos4 - Medium I will preface this review by stating that I am not a graphic artist and I have the artistic ability of a common garden rock. I did not get this tablet for doing artwork. As such, I have a different perspective on this product than the majority of people who buy an Intuos4.

I am very new to working with tablets and I started with a basic Bamboo small. This was a great little tablet, but the important word there was "little". I upgraded to an Intuos4 Medium because I wanted a bigger tablet, and I have been delighted with it. I do not use this tablet in the way a true artists would use it, but I have gained a deep appreciation for it nevertheless.

Because of the work I do, I use computers very frequently. I use them at home too, which is where I've attached my Intuos4. I am always looking for ways to make computing more comfortable, and on a whim I tried tablets. I discovered that, for me, tablet pens are more pleasant with which to work than mice.

The Intuos, in particular, is a good fit with an excellent digital pen that is designed well and fits my hand comfortably. The feel is right, and when writing the nib/tablet contact feels very much like writing on paper with a pencil. There are multiple nibs too, as well as additional pens for purchase, that make finding the right combination easy. So far, I have used only the default nib that was in the pen when I opened the box, and I am satisfied.

There is also a mouse in the package that works for most generic purposes but I rarely touch it. It is a no-frills, three-button scrolling mouse that is actually not bad, but it is only used on the writing surface of the tablet.

My primary use of this tablet is for writing, not drawing, and I have found the handwriting recognition software that is activated with the driver install to be mostly reasonable with translating my chicken scratches. It does have a bad tendency, however, to translate my lowercase letter "b" to "6" or sometimes even "d". As a result of this and other minor quirks I have changed my writing mannerisms to give the software better accuracy, and these new mannerisms are so habitual that I find that when I am writing on paper I have carried these new habits with me to that medium.

The tablet is much more pressure sensitive than my Bamboo was and when I make an effort to either bear down or lighten up with the pressure I can see the difference. This is especially true when using artistry software like Corel Painter. For serious artists, the Intuos4 offers 2048 pressure levels which should suffice for most.

I've made no use of the buttons on my Intuos4 but I use the Touch Ring frequently for scrolling. This is an excellent substitute for a scroll wheel, though it is not critical for my uses.

The pen and tablet are NOT useful for everything. For example, it's a bad choice for playing FPS games like Unreal Tournament. For chess, sudoku, working in MS Word or even grunching numbers in a spreadsheet, it is very workable.

Ok, so why do I prefer this higher-end tablet over a Bamboo Fun? I tried a Bamboo Fun Pen and Touch, which is a tablet that is more in line with people of my skill level (rank beginner and home user). That said, I could not get comfortable with the Pen and Touch, and I feel the Intuos4 pen is a much better for for my hands. Also, the Touch portion was awkward for me. The Intuos4 just works better for me, plain and simple.

For a non-artist, the Intuos4 Medium Tablet is a high-dollar item that can possibly be looked at as an unnecessary expense. For me, though, it is a blessing in that it makes most tasks on the computer more comfortable and easy. I am hooked on this tablet and recommend it to anyone who is either a serious artist looking for a good digital tablet or someone like me who just wants to be comfortable while working on the computer. It is a serious input device and will change the way you interact with the computer.
text_fidelity_b: Wacom Intuos Intuos4 - Medium

text_fidelity_a:
Sony A90J 65 Inch TV: BRAVIA XR OLED 4K Ultra HD Smart Google TV with Dolby Vision HDR and Alexa Compatibility XR65A90J- 2021 Model The box took a big gouge in shipping (in just the original TV box), but the TV was fine, so packaging is probably adequate. Unboxing was easy and there was just a bit of styrofoam and minimal cardboard. Be careful with removing the television from the box, because these things are getting thin enough to be bent under their own weight.

It mounted fine on my old wall mount, but required a different screw size. The screws from my previous setup were the wrong size, so you might want to check what you've got and order some so you don't have to wait around.

There isn't much thought put into cable management, so you'll have to come up with your own solution if you don't want cords visible. Power cord is in the lower right quadrant. Most of the other cords are in the lower left, as is a well hidden power button on the back left. The instructions are minimal. I tried hooking my receiver in as instructed to use the television speaker in place of my old center speaker, but it wouldn't work. It may have just been a clash of brands and standards, because every time I tried to switch to using the TV speakers in the options, it would shut off my Pioneer receiver instead. I ended up using the other speaker input, which did work. I can't believe we're in the 2020's and still cramming bare wires in as audio input. I've got a drawer full of various audio cables here.

Turning it on, I was greeted with setup options. The remote seems high quality, but I wish it had some air-remote functionality. Navigating menus with buttons can get a bit confusing. After getting it hooked up to wifi, I was off to YouTube to find something to make sure it was working right before I hooked everything else up. One of those HD coral reef relaxation videos was just the thing. The picture is vibrant! Bright and colorful. The bezels aren't small enough to tile these together, but are very small. My kids wouldn't let me change the video for hours. They just sat and watched the fish. I'm susceptible to the whine some televisions put out, and I've heard none of that. Worked great for video games, though I didn't try anything especially high end. Worked well for computer output. With the exception of that one audio jack compatibility issue, and the different sized screws, everything has worked as expected.

The screen is a speaker, like a modern smartphone. Sound is good, especially at frequencies you would hear from a center speaker. I definitely still wanted my subwoofer and side speakers to round things out, but it's really nice to have the voices from the television coming from where the faces are, not from some speaker below the television.

I don't have a different brand of 2021 television to compare it to, but my impression is that there is a bit of a premium for the brand name, but it's a very nice product. This was certainly an upgrade for me. A lot of progress has been made in the 8 years since I last upgraded.
text_fidelity_b: Sony A90J 65 Inch TV: BRAVIA XR OLED 4K Ultra HD Smart Google TV with Dolby Vision HDR and Alexa Compatibility XR65A90J- 2021 Model

UGREEN Lightning to USB Cable Data Syncing Charging Cord Compatible for iPhone 7,7plus,6S,6 Plus,iPhone5s,5c,5,iPad Mini,Mini 2,Air Etc MFI Certified (5ft, Silver) I have only recently started using UGREEN cables and so far every one of their cables I have used has been a top-notch product. I was interested to see how well their lightning cable would work out for me and, based on my experiences with their other cables I expected this cable to be excellent. I have not been disappointed.

First things first – this is an Apple-certified cable which is not insignificant. Because it is certified it will work right with your Apple device and the device will not complain about it being an unrecognized cable. If you have used cheaper cables that do not come with a certification you have seen the warning messages that appear when you connect it. This one will not cause that problem which is good right out of the box.

This cable seems to be well made and so far I have found no issues with build quality or assembly. The insulation is nice and thick and it securely attached on both ends so it will not pull away from the plugs. Each plug is shielded in an aluminum sheath which protects the plug and makes it a little easier to grip. I have the 5’ version of this cable which is nice; I like that I have a little more leeway with the extra length of the cable.

There’s something I want to emphasize about this cable which many might not consider or may think is insignificant. UGREEN has put their name right on the plug ends, where it is easy to see and read. This says that they believe in this product enough to brand it, which is actually uncommon. Most of the cables on my desk are not branded so it is very nice being able to identify a cable by manufacturer. When one goes bad, if it is not branded it is difficult to know where that cable came from. The very best micro USB cable I own is by UGREEN and because it is branded it is very easy for me to identify in the tangle on my desk. Now I can tell which lightning cable is theirs too.

I have not had this cable long enough to see how well it will hold up over time but in the time I have had it, it has been reliable and compatible. I like the extra length too which gives me some flexibility when figuring out where to put it and the device I connect to it.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: UGREEN Lightning to USB Cable Data Syncing Charging Cord Compatible for iPhone 7,7plus,6S,6 Plus,iPhone5s,5c,5,iPad Mini,Mini 2,Air Etc MFI Certified (5ft, Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG 75-Inch Class QLED 4K The Frame LS03B Series, Quantum HDR, Art Mode, Anti-Reflection Matte Display, Slim Fit Wall Mount Included, Smart TV w/ Alexa Built-In (QN75LS03BAFXZA, Latest Model) I am using this TV as my primary PC monitor. Since I don't have my PC stationed at a desk but rather use a wireless keyboard and mouse to remotely sit where I want to, the screen can be on my wall and I can comfortably sit back in my La-Z-Boy recliner several feet away while doing work, surfing the web, gaming, or whatever. This screen is really perfect for this, with a 120 hertz rate and 4k graphics. And of course it still maintains all the regular functionality of a TV as well.

I primarily use my computer to illustrate books for my day job, and this screen really makes my illustrations look great! Set to "Graphics" mode (rather than "Entertain" mode) the colors are true and the shadows retain great detail; the highlights are smooth, and clean. The color profile is easy to adjust. I really appreciate all of this very much. In the "Entertain" mode, the colors are amped up and the graphics are sharpened, etc. This is nice for watching films and gaming, but for doing graphics work it's absolutely necessary to have the colors and details represented accurately. The excellent anti-reflection and anti-glare features are also extremely helpful in this regard.

The native speakers are about what you would expect; they aren't amazing, but they aren't really all that bad for what this TV is intended to be either. It's really all about the screen. I personally don't care too much about the speakers, because 95% of the time that I use the screen I'm wearing headphones anyway so that I don't disturb my family. But if you're a real audiophile and that sort of thing is important to you, I would suggest you get some nice speakers to go with the TV, because the built-in speakers are clearly only meant to be just good enough to pass muster, and aren't anything to be wowed by.

For me, it's really nice that it doubles as a picture frame when I'm not actively using it for anything else. I have loaded an assortment of my own favorite photographs and illustrations for it to cycle through, and they look really great on this screen, but you can also access a fairly good assortment of art through the TV itself. This turns what is typically a bit of an eyesore in my opinion (I don't like the intrusive look of too much electronic technology in my home) into a lovely, active decoration instead.

I have not ordered a decorative frame to customize it; the reviews on those seem to indicate that they are perhaps overpriced and fragile, and I think it would be easy enough to make my own anyway, which I plan to do. I think having a frame on it would just be the cherry on top, so to speak.

And to reassure anyone who is wondering about the review that said this is the 2021 model, I think there must have been some confusion on one end or the other, because I definitely received the 2022 model that I ordered.

It came with the "Slim-Fit Wall Mount" included in the box (it's in the Styrofoam packing; I think another reviewer might have just not seen it, as it's not very large and it weighs much less than you might expect) along with a decent length of "One Invisible Connection" cable to attach it to the "One Connect Box" controller. This cable is just silver braid with a clear coating on it to help it blend in better than a regular black plastic cable. It serves as a power source as well as controlling the TV, so there's no bundle of unsightly cables hanging down from the screen.

The connect box replaces the usual bulk of the TV, which is what allows the screen to hang so flat on the wall like a regular picture frame. To use the TV, you'll need to position the One Connect box where you can use the remote to control it. It can be positioned anywhere so long as it's within reach of the cable. You can buy longer "One Invisible Connection" cables if necessary. The one that was included was long enough for my needs.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG 75-Inch Class QLED 4K The Frame LS03B Series, Quantum HDR, Art Mode, Anti-Reflection Matte Display, Slim Fit Wall Mount Included, Smart TV w/ Alexa Built-In (QN75LS03BAFXZA, Latest Model)

text_fidelity_a:
1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver I returned these because of a software bug with ANC - and also because the call quality was terrible.

These phones stood out for being wireless with active noise cancellation (ANC) AND pass through (so you can hear ambient sounds for safety in the City). Unfortunately, those features are the weak points of the headphones - to the point that I found I would never use the pass through and often didn't bother with the ANC.

SOUND QUALITY: VERY GOOD - EXCEPT - they tend to exaggerate the mid base a little which can make vocals - especially male vocals sound a little unclear. Listening to the same music on speakers vs the headphones, it was just plane more real sounding and pleasant on good speakers. High standard, I know. Other headphones don't have that particular problem (though may have others - like weak bass or sibilant highs). I haven't heard that many competing models, so I don't know how they compare to sennheiser or bose or anyone else in the same price class. At least others have an app with equalization (Jabra, Jaybird).

Bug w. ANC: Sometimes it would say it's on when it's off and vice-versa.

ANNOYING THING: When you engage the pass-through, it has a voice prompt that tells you the pass through is engaged. Since often I switch on the pass through when it's important to hear something, the several seconds it takes to make its silly announcement means I miss part of what I was trying to hear! I found I would always just yank one plug out of my ear instead and get the instant feedback. ALSO - this thing takes FOREVER to turn off. You have to hold hold hold and finally it announces it's powering off. Combined with poor power indicator light - this is just annoying.

NOTE: This is not a defect, but just poor design... There is NO WAY to activate Google Assistant or Siri with These. Even my cheapo earbuds let you use one of the buttons to summon Google. Without that, how are you supposed to make voice calls? I have to pull out my phone to make calls. Foo.

Combined with atrocious call quality (I could hear them, but the person on the other end is always mishearing words or saying WHAT? WHAT?), these are DOA for me.

ONE LAST THING: The APP is garbage. Just pointless.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver

text_fidelity_a: StarTech.com 2 Port USB DVI KVM Switch with DDM Fast Switching Technology and Cables - Dual Port DVI USB KVM Switch - DDM KVM Switch (SV231DVIUDDM) If you remember the old game unit switches that allowed you to use multiple devices on one television set, this is like that, only for two computers sharing one monitor, keyboard, mouse, and other peripherals. The simple switch box connects to your monitor ("console") via the kind of cord with plugs on both ends you currently use to connect your monitor to your computer. (You will need an extra cord like this for the the purpose--not included. If you don't have a spare lying around, you should order one with the unit.) You will need the cords you are currently using for each of the two computers to connect them to the box. There are four USB sockets in the "console" section of the box. You plug your keyboard, mouse, and anything else you want to share between the two computers into those. (By the way, KVM stands for Keyboard, Video,Mouse.) The unit is powered, and offers multiple plug styles for international use. There is a place to plug in speakers and a mike for each computer. This switch has made it possible for me to streamline my office space considerably. Previously, I had two monitors, two keyboards, and two mice. It was very awkward. I kept my old computer because it has Adobe CS4, which is fine for my needs and saves me the $50 a month the Creative Cloud would cost. I have not used it much, though. Firing up the old machine was just too much trouble. This new arrangement allows me to flip a switch and access programs I have not been able to use in a long time.
text_fidelity_b: StarTech.com 2 Port USB DVI KVM Switch with DDM Fast Switching Technology and Cables - Dual Port DVI USB KVM Switch - DDM KVM Switch (SV231DVIUDDM)

text_fidelity_a:
MAKTAR Qubii Duo USB-C Flash Drive(White Without microSD), Auto Backup While Charging, MFi Certified Compatible with iPhone/iPad/Android, Photo Storage/Stick with File Organizer APP THINGS YOU'LL NEED THAT ARE NOT INCLUDED:
----------------------------------------------------------
1. Your own micro SD card, up to 2tb.
2. A power adapter that has a usb-c port. The Qubii will be plugged into this adapter.
3. A usb-c to usb-c cable. To connect from the Qubii to the usb-c port of your Android phone.
4. A usb-c to Apple lightning if you'll be using an iPhone.

SOME NOTEWORTHY INFO:
---------------------------------
* This is a good idea, now that Google Photos is no longer unlimited.
* It basically backs-up every folder that has an image. There doesn't seem to be a way to choose which folders you want it to back-up. I only need my main camera folder to get backed-up, but oh well, backing up too much is better than too little.
* Once you disconnect from power adapter, you can use the Qubii as OTG storage. You'll need to turn on OTG storage in your system settings. If you have a case on your phone, you'll probably never bother to use it as OTG because you'll need to remove the case.
* Every time you want to transfer files to your PC, NAS, etc., you'll need to remove the micro sd card if your pc doesn't have a usb-c port. My PC does not, so I use a usb to usb-c adapter. This eliminates the hassle of having to take out micro sd cards, dealing with card readers, etc.
* After you transfer everything safely to your pc, if you delete the files on the micro SD card to clear space, the Qubii still maintains its count. So even if these files are still on your phone, it will not re-download them again.

In conclusion, how accurate and precise this system is remains to be seen. So far, it has backed up everything I need it to. I know people complain of missing files, not everything getting backed-up, etc. Most of these complaints revolves around people using iPhones. But we'll see, time will tell. As of now, this is 5-Stars!
text_fidelity_b: MAKTAR Qubii Duo USB-C Flash Drive(White Without microSD), Auto Backup While Charging, MFi Certified Compatible with iPhone/iPad/Android, Photo Storage/Stick with File Organizer APP

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic True Wireless Earbuds | Bluetooth Earbuds|IPX4 Water Resistant | Small, Lightweight | Long Battery Life, Alexa Compatible | RZ-S300W (White) I've been a fan of Panasonic's consumer electronics since their camcorder days, so I was excited to try these! I've owned many of the cheap Chinese wireless earbuds, and generally sound is good enough for music or listening to videos but I've never found one with a microphone decent enough for sound quality outside of the major brands (Apple, Samsung, etc).
Well, I'm happy to say these Panasonic 'buds don't skimp! They don't cost as much as the big players but the sound quality both for listening and microphone use is head and shoulders over the cheap knock offs. The noice cancelling feature is pretty amazing as well, and overall I'm very pleased with the feature set and quality of those features. But here's the caveat:
The ergonomics aren't great. Touch sensitive buds are difficult for me because I'm the kind of person who moves around a lot and needs to adjust my earbuds to keep them from falling out. But touch sensitivity means sometimes I'm accidentally activating things when I don't want to. I also didn't find some of the features intuitive and had to learn how to use them properly (changing noise cancelling modes for example). They also have rather bright blinking LEDs but you'll only notice that in a dark room. All in all, this is a good product that could be made better in a second edition. For the price, I think it fits squarely between the polished big name brands and the cheap knock offs. This is a good product, it works and doesn't exactly what it says. But it isn't perfect.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic True Wireless Earbuds | Bluetooth Earbuds|IPX4 Water Resistant | Small, Lightweight | Long Battery Life, Alexa Compatible | RZ-S300W (White)

Sound quality is better than the speaker on my smartphone, but clearly worse than $30 portable Bluetooth speakers (like the Oontz Curve), which offer more volume, more bass, and cleaner sound. Unlike most portable Bluetooth speakers, this one does not have a microphone, so you cannot pair it with your smartphone for use as a speakerphone. Maximum volume is fairly low, but that does help with battery life and also reduces the chance of distortion at higher volumes. Most good sounding Bluetooth speakers cost $30 and up, so temper your expectations for this cheap product and you'll probably be happy.

Samson LTS50 Laptop Stand (SALTS50), Packs, Black I purchased this to support a [[ASIN:B00ND1KHY2 Mackie Mix Series Mix12FX -Watt 12-Channel Mixer]], which it easily does. What impressed me the most is the construction. I had been using a music stand with the tray perpendicular to the ground and it worked, but was not nearly as stable as this stand. Moreover, I looked at a few other brands, but most were cheaply made.

Here are a few things that set this one apart: first, the clamping mechanisms are quick release type and not the cheesy knobs that every other stand I tried employs. Second, if you are considering this for a truly heavy device like a projector the pins for the support pole guarantee that it will be supported. Frankly, the pins are probably never going to be needed because the main release mechanisms hold firmly.

Dimensions are:
Tray: 15 9/16 x 10 7/8 inches with lips along the widths top and bottom.
Stand: adjusts from 23 to 53 inches - this is ideal if you are a keyboardist or drummer who wants to control your instrument and mics via a mixer because the height range is perfect for most scenarios.
Footprint: 25 inches between tripod feet points.

This also comes with a sticky silicone pad that measures 12 x 7 5/78 inches to hold a mixer or laptop firmly in place. My Mackie mixer did not budge when it was placed on the pad and the table tilted 30 degrees.

Finally, I purchased a [[ASIN:B000XZYXTG Hamilton Carrying Bag for KB50 & KB990 Series Stands]] that easily holds and protects this stand. I recommend it if you do opt for this model.
text_fidelity_b: Samson LTS50 Laptop Stand (SALTS50), Packs, Black

Canon Powershot A1200 12.1 MP Digital Camera with 4x Optical Zoom (Silver) (OLD MODEL) OK, here are the facts: my other (similar) camera developed a glitch -- it will not allow me to delete photos without loooooong delays. So I went in search of an inexpensive replacement camera. I settled on this Canon.

I did so with trepidation because some of the reviews were lukewarm at best. Yet other reviewers loved it. (This, by the way, is what makes horse races!) So I thought I would take a chance.

Here is why I am happy with my choice: (1) the viewer seems larger than its dimensions suggest; (2) the camera fits in my shirt pocket; (3) the pics are crisp indoors and out; (4) the on-off button is clearly marked and the shot button is nice and robust. For me, these features are all I need. To be sure, the camera has a few video bells and whistles -- I'll try those one of these days. No rush.

A Con: the shot button takes a little getting used to, since it appears to have two stages to it. If you just press and disengage, nothing will happen. It requires a little patience and then it will take the picture. I can live with that idiosyncrasy.

Another Con: no internal memory. You must purchase an SD card before you can use the camera. This too I have accepted, because having pics on cards does make it easy to load them into PCs and laptops.

If you are looking for a simple "point-and-shoot" camera that will also perform other tricks if you are of a mind, go for it!

I can't guarantee that this printer is going to be any better in the long run, but the set-up actually works pretty well if you use the standard version, not the WPS... and I'm getting way ahead of myself on this one.

To begin with, the printer requires a lot of time for set-up. You're not going to be doing this on the fly, so set aside an hour or so to: 1) remove all the tape of which there is much, 2) read over the instructions 3) install the ink, 4) run a print alignment 5) set up your wireless connection (about which more in a moment) 6) install the software (which takes a good 15 minutes or more), and 7) put the machine (and yourself) through its paces. Yeah, it's going to take a while.

Now I know you can read about the features on your own, so I'm here to tell you about the things that work for me and those that don't. First off, the wireless set-up is confusing. Choose Standard instead of WPS and save yourself some headaches unless you're a computer whiz kid. After the third error message in the WPS set-up I went to standard, entered my pass code and had the connection up and running in about a minute.

Once that was done and the software was installed I fired up the Canon Image Garden. First I scanned an image and attempted to rotate, crop and fix any deficiencies I found. The scan was over sharp and looked a bit jagged, but a little fiddling with the Canon software fixed that. Canon software also rotated and cropped perfectly. One really nice feature is that they remind you to put the printing side of the paper down in the paper cassette. How many pieces of paper will that save?

The biggest complaint I had was that it didn't give me a choice of which paper cassette to use for printing, so I got a ridiculously truncated image on the first try. I believe it chooses the paper based on the size of the image, which I get, but at the same time that limits flexibility in printing. I opened another photo processing program and it allowed me to print from whatever cassette I liked. Coupled with a better suite of applications for correction and enhancement, I think it's safe to say that I'll be using the Canon software almost never.

Printing on plain paper is clearly not going to be as satisfactory as it is on glossy, but in some cases I found it surprisingly good, good enough to give you an idea of what sort of image you're going to end up with when you switch to photo paper. It's also more than good enough for printing out emails and web pages.

Scanning and printing are both pretty fast, another plus. And the copy function works pretty seamlessly without any sort of computer interface. Just punch a couple of buttons and Bob's your uncle! It does take a bit of time to warm up and is a little noisy but no more so than any Canon printer I've ever used. It's not bothersome, in my opinion. You might feel otherwise.

Inks are easy to install, but you'll find refills pricey, no question. I suspect off-brand ones are available or will be soon enough.

In short, it's a good, inexpensive printer for a home or home office. Use photo paper and settings and get the full quality the MG5420 is capable of producing; I think it's pretty remarkable. The photos I printed out are as good as or in one case, better than the original. That's a powerful recommendation in my book.
text_fidelity_b: Canon Office Products MG5420 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier

Pen in the photo for size reference, along with the box it came in.

Unboxing was “frustration free” as advertised. I recycled my Logitech cord that connected to my desktop and inserted the USB receiver in it and it worked.

I plugged in the Micro USB charging cable to the keyboard and mouse. Only one Micro USB charging cable came with the combo so I used an extra Android Micro USB charging cable to charge both at the same time.

I was able to use the keyboard and mouse in a few moments. My computer automatically updated the files needed in a few minutes.

All in all the unboxing and set up was quick and effortless. Now I am going to explore the keyboard.

This keyboard has no number side keyboard that makes it smaller.

It has a blue function key to access page up, page down, home, and end, on the lower right where the left, right, up, down keys are.

Along the top with the F keys are blue function commands:

Escape has “Media” – when pressed opened Wave Pad, a NCH program I have installed.

F1 has an >/||, which did nothing when pressed

F2 has |<<, which did nothing when pressed

F3 has >>|, which did nothing when pressed

F4 has a speaker symbol )x, That mutes sound

F5 has a speaker symbol - which lowers volume

F6 has a speaker symbol + which increases volume

F7 has a symbol for home, which opens a new browser tab

F8 has a symbol of a magnifying glass that opens a search side window and uses Bing for search, when I clicked on one of the search results it opened a new Chrome tab. I had Chrome already opened.

F9 has a symbol for a folder, which did nothing when pressed

F10 has a symbol for power which turned off my computer. Since I had programs opened my computer asked for permission so I canceled.

F11 has “insert” on it which is pretty self explanatory

F 12 has “PrtSc” for print screen

The action on the keyboard is nice and a lot quieter than the Logitech keyboard I am replacing. The mouse action is good and also quiet.

For less than $23 this is a good keyboard and mouse. I never used the number keys on the side of my Logitech keyboard, which needed batteries, as did the mouse that came with it. The mouse had begun to do double clicks when I clicked once and the keyboard “enter” would stay down. That's why I replaced them for this Arteck Keyboard and Mouse combo. To be able to stop buying and replacing batteries and the small space it takes up, along with it is quiet, makes my money well spent.

text_fidelity_a:
Pentax K100D Super 6.1MP Digital SLR Camera Shake Reduction and 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Lens First of all, I would like to start with highly recommending this camera to ANYONE who wants premium image quality with expandability, power and flexibility.

Pentax is one of the only companies out there that is driven entirely by photography and NOT by a marketing department that makes outrageous claims. To this end, even this, their lowest-end camera, is PACKED with premium features. Let's take a look at them:

1. Dust Reduction: Dust WILL get into your camera! This keeps it off of the sensor and increases the time inbetween cleanings.

2. Shake Reduction: It's good for a couple of stops of shooting leeway and you get it with every lens you use. Other companies build their systems into the lenses, meaning ONE lens can cost as much or more than the camera, itself! Lens-based anti-shake systems are more effective at long zoom than body-based systems, but unless you're rich, you won't be able to afford a suite of good lenses! With this camera, you can use ANY Pentax lens and get anti-shake.

3. AA batteries: Proprietary battery packs are NO GOOD. Hmmm, if you're on a shoot and your pack dies, you're not taking ANY photos unless you get a spare, right? With this camera, pick up some 2500mAh Ni-MH AA's and you can afford to get three sets. However, the power drain is so small, you might not need more than one set.

4. 6 MP sensor: Don't EVER get trapped in the megapixel hype. Megapixels mean nothing in the DSLR game, except for noise issues. Let me explain. The sensor sizes on almost all DSLRs (except for $5000 full-frame pro cameras) are APS-sized, meaning the sensor size on this camera and the Nikon D300 are very nearly the same dimensions. This means that photosensors on the chip have to be made smaller to get more pixels...meaning that the closer together/smaller sites are LESS light sensitive and they will also interfere with each other. 6 MP is a perfect sweet spot for noise and image sharpness. You get a base ISO of 200, meaning your camera is TWICE as sensitive to light as one with a base ISO of 100! This camera records color accurately and makes prints up to 8.5"x11" with no problem.

This camera has huge features and, even with the release of the K20D and K200D cameras, still maintains a good feature/image quality set with a proven CCD sensor and a suite of easy-to-learn features and settings. I LOVE this camera and even though I have a K200D for the weather sealing and larger burst capacity, the K100D super is the camera I ALWAYS take with me in trips. You're better off getting this camera plus a really nice lens and a 360FZ flash than a more expensive camera with a base kit lens and no external flash.

Believe me, this camera's quality will not fail to impress you and it will grow with you. It can use ANY lens its bigger brothers can and it uses them effortlessly.

A superb camera and one for the record books!
text_fidelity_b: Pentax K100D Super 6.1MP Digital SLR Camera Shake Reduction and 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Lens

Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer) First, let me preface that I in NO way count myself a photog. I am just a shutter bug who has been firing frames almost non-stop since the age of 18. I learned on my dad's 'old' Nikon SLR with an f/1.2 lens. The Nikon SLRs/DSLRs I have owned are: N50, N60, N55, N80 and D50. My N50 ad N80 had the best lenses. The N60 and N55 were not as great and the D50 was a fabulous entry-level digital. The only medium format camera I own is my Holga. But hey, unlike the photographer at Portrait Innovations, at least I know 'medium format' does not refer to the number of megapixels at which I am shooting. As for my working knowledge, I had three semesters of photography in college. I can process/print both B&W and color film. (Not that that does me any good these days LOL) I can shoot completely 'manual' and I have stood among many pro photographers on the bridge at sunset, waiting for the color to be just right on Half Dome. (My Bogen tripod was way too heavy to be practical for an amateur but it gave me street credit.) So, in a nut shell, I shoot by the 'Sunny 16' rule. I know that opening my f-stop should increase my shutter speed give me a shorter depth of field; and, per the great Ansel Adams, f/8 is a proper exposure for all pictures.

That said, I hate my D3100.

I have had metering issues since I opened the box. I bought the camera so I could take 'even better' pictures of my infant son than I was getting from my D50. Ha. Joke was on me.

The contrast was BLINDING on the factory settings and every shot was over exposed. I have tried every metering option in the menu but the only changes I can achieve are under-exposure, blurred focus and missed shots. It's go high or go without.

I always lower my ISO to 100 when I'm outside because I crave rich color but it's just not there. I have tried Aperture Priority, Shutter Priority and Manual. Nothing. f/16 over my film speed on a sunny day. That's supposed to work! I have used it on many a 'less complicated' camera and achieved photos that make jaws drop. Well, there's no jaw dropping with this camera.

The metering overrides my manual choices every time. It's like I'm having a battle of wits with my camera. :( It reminds me of the days when Kodak was marketing 800-speed film as a universal, never-miss-a-shot solution to all your photo woes. Bleh. Just because there's always an image doesn't mean it's the RIGHT exposure.

I get that being an entry-level/made-for-the-masses DSLR really does mean it's a glorified point-and-shoot but it should preform at least as well as it's predecessors. Honestly, I got far more reliable results from my Canon SureShot and a roll of Kodak 100.

My expectation for a camera is that the image should be very close to perfect when the shutter closes. I know there's always room for improvement before printing but that's the art of photography. The hours I spend working on my photos after the shot should be to make them pop. Instead, my time is spent trying to rescue precious memories.

If you are considering this camera as your first DSLR because you think it will improve your skills, skip it. Invest in an equally expensive point-and-shoot that will give you all the same manual controls and preform much better in low-light situations. The D3100 does not live up to the standards of a Nikon SLR.

I gave it a second star because my son pulled mine off the counter about a year after I bought it and although the case cracked, it didn't seem to hurt the camera. Unfortunately, it impact didn't help it, either. (Yes, I was actually hopeful.)
text_fidelity_b: Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

It's such a shame that the manufacturer decided to save money on image quality and it's a weird business decision that makes an otherwise fun and well built product useless.

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser PXC 450 Active Noise-Canceling Headphones I spend a great deal of time in a computer lab where there is literally over 1,000 running systems. In this environment, ear protection isn't absolutely necessary but without it there's some discomfort with which to deal because of all the fans in these systems and the requisite air handling units. I already have a pair of Bose QC-15 headphones but I am not a huge fan, so I recently purchased a pair of Sennheiser PXC-450 headphones for use in this environment. After an initial break-in period, I have come to really appreciate them.

This is going to be a comparative review, though primarily about the Sennheiser phones. Bose is generally regarded as the gold standard when it comes to ANC headphones, so matching the Sennheisers to the Bose is a good match-up. I'll break it all down into categories: Noise Canceling, Comfort, Sound Quality and Build Quality.

Noise Canceling:
Active noise canceling is THE primary feature of these phones and each has its strengths. Bose is, without question, the more capable ANC set when it comes to removing noise. This supremacy comes at a price though - because of the aggressiveness of their ANC, the wearer often feels a "pressure" on the ears when using the phones, something not present with the Sennheiser set which is close to Bose's level of canceling. Where Bose went to extremes to eliminate noise, Sennheiser went with the thought of "good enough for most". To be sure, both sets do a nice job of eliminating low frequency noise, enough to make air travel more pleasant if you dislike the rumble of plane engines.

They work in the car too (if you're not driving). I tried both sets in a moving vehicle and all do a fine job of eliminating road and engine noise. In fact, it was quiet to the point of eerie in the car. So, if you're a passenger on a long trip, either of these will work to suit your needs.

For the Sennheisers, you don't have to use ANC to listen to music as they provide the ability to override ANC and work like normal headphones. Bose, on the other hand, is an all-or-nothing deal and requires ANC to be on when listening to anything at all.

And that brings up a nice little feature on the Sennheisers - the "talk-thru" function, which allows a listener to cut off all sound and turn on a small microphone so that one can carry on a conversation without having to remove the headphones. No other headset I have ever used has this feature and it has already proven to be a handy tool.

Both sets require a single AAA battery to provide ANC. The battery life is definitely better with the Bose - mine last about a week between needing new batteries, whereas the Sennheiser set needs a new battery every other day.

Comfort:
The Sennheisers are the most comfortable headphones I have ever worn - period. The padding is buttery soft and they fit over my ears with no issue. Other reviewers have said that it seems like they just melt into your head, and that's a very accurate way to describe them. The Bose are nearly as comfortable, though they are slightly smaller.

Where the Sennheisers have a slight comfort disadvantage is actually in their size. These are big headphones and when they are worn around the neck instead of on the ears, they tend to rub on the neck and sometimes (depending on what you're doing) they can get in the way. If you take them off, or don't wear them around your neck, there's nothing about which to complain.

Sound Quality:
Sennheiser has always had premium sound, and the PXC-450 headphones demonstrate why they are the champs when it comes to quality sound. Though not audiophile phones, the PXC-450 brings awesome sound quality even at low volumes, with very full midrange and decent bass. The Bose sound great, except that the bass is too rich and without an equalizer in the mix the bass is enough to give me a headache over extended periods.

Build Quality:
I have not had the Sennheiser set very long but so far I have had no trouble with them. They feel rugged and sturdy, though they are mostly plastic so they do scratch and twist easily. The cord is heavy gauge wire, a welcome improvement over the cabling on Sennheiser sets I have worn in the past. The Bose set is a little more flimsy, with lesser gauge wire.

In summary, I find that the Sennheiser PXC-450 headphones are a better product than the Bose QC-15 headphones. They sound great, feel comfortable and they do a fine job of canceling noise. Bose does have better ANC and if that is the main thing you need and you don't mind the sensation of pressure they put on the ears then Bose is a better choice, but in almost every other aspect the Sennheisers bring more to the table.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser PXC 450 Active Noise-Canceling Headphones

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote Logitech, Programmable Remote (Silver) I recently purchased this to replace a lost remote for a piece of high end integrated amp. As with most things in the audiophile world, a replacement for this simple 6 button remote was way overpriced ($105) for what it is. So I was pleased to find that my amplifier was supported by the Logitech 650.

My biggest gripe is nearly a dealbreaker. After setting it up I went to use it on my integrated amplifier to raise the volume a little bit. The problem was that I couldn't just give the volume button a quick tap to turn up the volume a little bit. A quick tap of the volume raised the volume a significant amount whereas the original amp controller allowed me to make volume changes in small increments. After some searching I found that I just had to adjust the IR repeat length in the controller setup.

Problem solved, right? Wrong.

First issue was the manual being outdated. The frustration started when I tried following the steps in the manual. The first step was "Click Troubleshoot at the top of the Harmony Remote Software window". The problem was that there was no Troubleshoot button anymore. They had updated the software but didn't update the manual. Eventually I found the new location in the software where you can lower the repeats. The default was set to 1 so I lowered it to 0 (the lowest setting on the 0-4 scale). I saved my changes and after waiting for the remote to update I tried it again and it still was making large volume changes. With the remote already set to the lowest setting the only way I can make small adjustments to volume is to press the volume button and cover the IR emitter on the remote extremely fast so the volume change signal only gets sent out for a quick burst. I'm talking ninja fast. This is extremely annoying and tricky to get the hang of.

PROS
-Price
-Device Compatibility

CONS
-Can't make small volume changes
-Outdated Manual (they updated the software but didn't update the PDF manual with new instructions for the new software). This causes some serious frustration when you are instructed in Step 1 to press a Troubleshooting button that no longer exists.

Final thoughts... I bought this to mainly do one thing. Change volume and input selection on my integrated amp. The inability to change the volume in small increments is a constant annoyance. It should be something that can be fixed with a software or firmware update.

AKIIO Akiio-Blue Waterproof LED Stick, 4 Light Settings, 2-100% Gradient Brightness, Blue, USB Rechargeable Battery, 5-Hour Charge, Includes Wrist Strap, Stand, 3M Adhesive Magnetic Clip It's a rechargeable glow stick or light wand that looks like something out of 2001 A Space Odyssey. What's not to like about that? It comes with a little stand to make it a table light, a wrist holder to make it a jogging light, and a magnetic holder to make it a strip light wherever you might need some extra illumination. It's also fun to just wave about while dancing or goofing around outside at night. There's four different light modes - white, cool blue, warm, and flashing, which can be shifted by tapping one end of the wand. The brightness can also be adjusted from very bright to nightlight dim by holding down that same end. So this really is a versatile lighting tool that goes beyond the traditional flashlight.

There are a few flaws but they are fairly minor. The instructions are minimal and it took me a little bit to figure out that you turn it off by tapping through all four lighting modes. An on/off switch along with a dimmer knob would have been the more traditional approach but that would have clashed with the sleek styling. So I can live with the finger tapping method. I'm still not sure I have the wrist strap set correctly but since I don't jog it's not a big deal to me. The other minor flaw is that the usb recharging cord has a different plug in than the other rechargeable devices I have. That means one more cord to keep track of but again that's not a big deal. Just looking at this thing makes me smile. That and its versatility far outweigh the minor negatives mentioned here so I happily give it five stars.
text_fidelity_b: AKIIO Akiio-Blue Waterproof LED Stick, 4 Light Settings, 2-100% Gradient Brightness, Blue, USB Rechargeable Battery, 5-Hour Charge, Includes Wrist Strap, Stand, 3M Adhesive Magnetic Clip

text_fidelity_a:
Netgear WGR614 Wireless-G Router We bought this Netgear WGR614 router back in March 2006. It installed somewhat easily and except for a little problem with the wireless PC card for the laptop (wouldn't be recognized at first but easily corrected) we had pretty stable use for about a year. Then we began to have connection problems. The connection would get slower and slower until internet pages would just not load, resulting in repeated "page cannot be displayed" errors. Powering down and restarting the router, modem and computer seemed to correct the issue. But as of this morning the router appears to have completely died. Powering down and restarting does nothing, the internet connection cannot be re-established. We can connect the desktop directly to the cable modem but for now the laptop is without connection, making for some unhappy family members here.

As of right now I don't know if we'll be buying another Netgear router & wireless PC card. The life expectancy of Netgear products does not appear to be all that great. Looking at some of the reviews we appear to be quite lucky that we got as much time out of the router as we did. Still I'm not in the mood to be shopping for a new router every 1.5 years or less. Hopefully there is a good router out there that can last at least two years.
text_fidelity_b: Netgear WGR614 Wireless-G Router

Belkin Verve Folio Case with Stand for Samsung Galaxy Tab 10.1inch (Black) My favorite types of cases are the rigid style that grab onto the edges of the device and do not increase the width or length of the device significantly. This is sort of a hybrid between that style and Belkin's ultrathin folio style.

That's because this one has a "pocket" for the device just like the soft ultrathins, which means you see the screen through a well placed cutout. It also has holes cut for the buttons, lenses, and ports. It is smaller from a length and width perspective than the ultrathin, but a bit deeper because the cover is thicker. It also has cleaner lines, although not as clean as some hard cases.

It also has an elastic strap attached to the cover that can be turned around to hold the case shut. Only time will tell if that stays nice and tight or ends up sagging after use. Really, it doesn't need to be used often as the case will mostly stay shut by itself.

The one thing I don't like is the way you fold the front cover behind the back: it sort of seems too stiff, as if you're not really supposed to. It also folds at both joints, which keeps it from lying completely flat. The ultrathin folio has it beat in that case, although I like the Verve in better in most other ways.

A nice case for your tablet.

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229 Wow, before saying anything, the screen on this laptop is stunning; bright and sharp. It is not the first nice thing I noticed about the laptop. Out of the box, it has a solid, perhaps a little heavy feel. It has a matte crosshatched finish which is not my favorite, but looks classy enough. The basic shape is elegant, it is thin and sleek and satisfying in the hand.

Keyboard/Touchpad

The keys are backlit, crisp to the touch and typing is easy. It has a slightly compressed full keyboard with a squeezed 10 key which is nice, and at least for my uses fine that the keys are 2/3rds their normal width. Keypad is sensitive but clicking works better than most and I have no problems with fine control of the cursor. The fingerprint reader is on the touchpad but does not affect usage and is a nice touch in general. All in all, inputs through keyboard, touchpad and touchscreen are perfect.

Screen

Like I said, once this one on, the screen is what stuck out for me. Wonderfully bright and crisp. Touch screen controls seem to work fine. Screen size is great. We watched a number of HD nature films on it and felt comfortable. The screen hinges completely around to create a tablet which I far prefer to swivel options. I also liked the way that it tents for movie and presentation viewing. Could not be happier with the screen.

CPU/Performance

This is a nice quick machine. SSD, i7 and plenty of RAM out of the box had it booting quick and I see no problems with performance. I would be amazed and happy to see it approach the 9 hours of battery life that it promises, we'll see about that over time. My son wanted to put it through the paces with STEAM games but I'm passing - It's mine, but it should handle most reasonable games although it is obviously not optimized for hard core gaming.

Summary

This is a well built, solid laptop. It has the makings for a great Netflix platform with it's screen and flexibility of viewing positions of the screen as well as crisp, bright HD. This is hands down the best laptop I have owned as a complete package.

Pros
+ Super Bright, HD screen
+ Nice crisp feel to the keyboard
+ Well powered for standard uses, SSD, i7 and RAM gives it enough muscle

Cons
-The design of the power cord and jack are disappointing, It looks spindly and its design encourages lateral pressures. I really wish more thought went into that.
-The pattern on the outside is not my favorite, but looks nice enough
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229

text_fidelity_a:

I used Amazon Prime Now to get the radio to me, in less than 1 hour (about 45 minutes) the delivery person was knocking on my door with my new receiver, wow, I was highly impressed and I will always check to see if Prime Now is available for all my deliveries from now on.....
So, the radio....
This receiver has a 4 gig SD card preloaded with every known frequency with text for the entire US and Canada. They have software called Sentinel you install on your PC and this is your gateway to all updates and firmware and it can control your radios SD card any way you like. Sentinel has an extensive database of all frequencies and let me say this again, all frequencies have text description included which is the most highly advanced scanner database system I have ever seen and I have owned scanner receivers most of my adult life, (long time)..
This is a digital receiver using the latest technology available. It can monitor any analog or digital TX (with some exceptions, like encrypted signals) and gives you extensive control over what you're listening to. There are FCC laws regarding what is legal and not legal to monitor and Uniden has got us right up to the maximum legally allowed to be monitored by civilians. If you are law enforcement persons you will have much more powerful receivers available to you capable of Cell phone conversation monitoring etc., things no civilian should even be interested in.
There is another version of this Uniden radio, the BCD536 which is a tabletop version. If you have large powerful outdoor weatherproof antennas the BCD536 is a good option and it is completely transferable to vehicle dash mount and back from your work desk to your vehicle.
I like this handheld BCD436 best personally for my purposes.
This is basically a plug and play receiver. It comes with 3 2300 milliamp rechargeable batteries, load those, charge them or just leave radio plugged in, enter your zip and you're in. Well theoretically that's how it works, in the real world? No.
When you first receive the radio I would suggest positioning yourself in front of your PC. Have the paper manual, the radio, you and your PC right there in front of you. Get ready to read and learn your radios keyboard layout and what these great, well thought out keys can do for you. You will learn, trust me, you will quickly come to love this radio.
Some cons:
No wall charger adopter included. You can charge from your PC's USB ports but you will need a wall charger with USB port. Most of us have several of these around the house from old cell phones etc. They work fine.
This unit should come with a nice wall charger adopter. That's really the only con, not to bad really.
Antennas:
Your ability to scan and receive signals on any scanner is proportionate to your antennas. The more robust and correct (correct meaning size, materials used etc).. You will need some nice antennas for this nice radio to increase your scanning powers. Amazon has some nice antennas, scannermaster.com has some also. Your local radio shop retailer will have some also. The included rubber ducky antenna is garbage, toss it from across the room to your garbage can, see if you can make a rim shot. Like I said, I have been playing with scanners for many years so I have many antennas to pick from.
Verdict:
This is without a doubt, the most powerful handheld scanning receiver available from any manufacturer. It is the luxury sedan of the scanning receiver world. It is easy and robust. It is backed up by Uniden's Sentinel software which will future proof your radio for many years to come.
I give Uniden 5 stars for this winner.
I give Amazon 5 stars for Prime Now 1 hour shipping, also a winner.

Edit:
Okay some people are wondering what the best accessories are for this receiver.
Go to scannermaster.com and look for the Austin Condor All-Band Portable BNC Antenna and the SpectrumForce Desk Mount for One Portable Scanner.
The Condor all band antenna is unsurpassed.
The desktop stand holds your handheld at the perfect viewing angle, you can listen and see all text clearly right beside your computer.
See my photos. The photos ended up sideways.... trying to fix this..... Amazon, can you turn my photos upright?
text_fidelity_b: Uniden BCD536HP HomePatrol Series Digital Phase 2 Base/Mobile Scanner with HPDB and Wi-Fi & (BC23A) Bearcat 15-Watt Amplified External Communications Speaker
