text_fidelity_a:
KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation) UPDATE 1/5/14: I'm downgrading my rating of this keyboard to three stars for one main reason: there are very sharp edges on the inside of the two sides of this split keyboard which can cut your wrists if you aren't careful. I put my mouse in between the two sides of the keyboard because that is the best position for it for me to prevent back and arm strain. Unfortunately, every time I use the mouse, my right wrist runs into the sharp edges of the inside of the right side of this split keyboard. To give you an idea how bad this sharpness is, I wear a [[ASIN:B008C27UPQ sport wristband]] to protect my wrist, and it is literally shredding from coming in contact with the knife-sharp plastic edge. I have tried putting duct tape over the sharp edge, but it won't stick to the plastic this keyboard is made of, and to add insult to injury, the tape looks awful.

Previous Review:

I recently had a bad flare-up of right arm pain from repetitive stress. I experimented to figure out which movements at my computer were hurting me the most, and I realized that reaching for the mouse was even more painful than keyboarding. As a result, I searched for keyboards here on Amazon with the potential to be divided in half, so that I could place my mouse right in front of me. That search led me to this keyboard.

This "freestyle" keyboard gives you the option to either leave the two sides hooked together and place it at a 45-degree angle on each side, or unhook the two sides totally. It is a simple procedure, no tools required, to unhook the two sides.

This product comes with instructions for putting the keyboard together from scratch, but everything came assembled except for mounting the padding that supposedly goes under your wrists--I have medium-sized hands, and the padding lands at the base of my hands, nowhere near my wrists. The padding also is not very thick, and I'm not sure why the manufacturer did not just go ahead and paste on the padding themselves--it's a hassle making sure it is totally straight before you stick it on. It can't be re-positioned if you mess up. Fortunately, I didn't mess up, and I don't have a huge need to support my wrists, so I am not downgrading my rating for that, but some consumers might want to know about it.

I really like the ability to put my mouse pad in between the two halves. This works as well as I had hoped to prevent the strain of reaching for the mouse constantly. The keys have a nice feel to them, as well. I am a touch typist, and I was very concerned at first that I would lose that ability on a strange keyboard. I have learned after multiple long days of using the keyboard that the trick is to get my fingers in the right position to begin with, such that my right pointer finger is on the J, and my left pointer finger is on the F. Even so, I currently hit false keys much more than normal. I hope that time and use will overcome this issue. I have ordered an additional one of these keyboards to hook up to my laptop so that I am always employing the same keyboarding reflexes, in order to more quickly retrain my brain.

This keyboard is certainly much more expensive than the $15-19 keyboards I've used forever, but will be well worth the price if it, as I think it will, helps prevent the excruciating pain of repetitive stress syndrome.

This keyboard is made so that the inner section can be elevated at either of two selected heights, or it can be fairly flat. This is useful for varying the position of the hands. As a physical therapist told me years ago, changing position and resting are crucial for preventing repetitive stress. I've tried all three levels, and I find the highest one the most comfortable.

Another plus of this keyboard is that I can now bilaterally employ a beneficial PT suggestion: I have for years placed a pillow under my right arm which is positioned against the arm of my [[ASIN:B000PWGZOI rolling office chair]]. This takes the strain off my arm and shoulder by bracing them. The fact that I'm using a pillow means that I am not in danger of damaging the brachial plexus nerve in the axilla (underarm), which can happen with hard objects like crutches. Previously, it never felt comfortable when I used a traditional keyboard to do this for my left arm, but with this keyboard, it does. Now, with both arms/shoulders braced, I find that it is much easier and even automatic to keep my back straight and my head up. It has greatly eased not just arm and hand strain, but back, shoulders and neck strain as well. In addition, I make a point to take my hands completely off the keyboard and mouse when reading, vs. keyboarding, and the pillows give me a comfortable place to elevate my hands, on the top of the pillow where it extends from beneath my underarm.

I rate this product as follows:
Ease of use: 4 stars (should improve with practice)
Functionality for preventing muscle strain: 5 stars
Comfort of use on wrist: 3 stars
Ease of assembly: 4 stars
Attractiveness of keyboard: 4 stars
text_fidelity_b: KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation)

text_fidelity_a:
MP3 Player with Bluetooth and WiFi, 4" Full Touch Screen MP4 MP3 Player with Spotify, Android Streaming Music Player with Pandora, Portable HiFi Sound Walkman Digital Audio Player with Speaker (White) Yes, the UI and apps are very clearly Android. No, it isn't a mini tablet.
Players like this are an interesting market that is hard to pin the audience down for. There are music players that are cheap on the market for those that would rather have a dedicated player (ie, not their phone). However the user interface tends to be wonky and slow, and newer generation features like bluetooth 5+ and streaming are often a mixed bag, if even available.
The idea behind players like this one, is that it is based on a supported operating system (Android, in this case) so it can play almost any format you throw at it, has plenty of support for popular streaming apps and features, as well as a familiar user interface that is already so polished, it seems silly to reinvent the wheel like the super cheap older media players.
Is it a mini tablet or phone without service? Not exactly. This is not a Google certified device, it does not have the play store or any Google apps on it. Unlike some other Android based players, I couldn't even get sideloaded apk files to install (it kept throwing errors at me). It seems like this device was purposely locked down to keep it an mp3 player. That's good in some ways, my kids aren't allowed unlimited screen time and their schools don't want them bringing smartphones around, so this is a strictly music-player oriented device (especially once you remove things like the browser for them, which it allows you to do). But I also know there are more capable players out there, some of which have quad DAC audio chips. Also, what happens when an app gets updated and goes out-of-date? Sometimes streaming services make changes and updated clients are required for it to work, however you are largely stuck with the version that this came with unless they issue a firmware update or something.
This is still cheaper than the higher end mp3 players that support high end DAC and app updates, but not by much. It seems to be a sort of in-between product. If you have a use for something like this, it could be a pretty good option. But if you're expecting a handheld tablet or alternative concept to an ipod touch, it is not exactly that.
text_fidelity_b: MP3 Player with Bluetooth and WiFi, 4" Full Touch Screen MP4 MP3 Player with Spotify, Android Streaming Music Player with Pandora, Portable HiFi Sound Walkman Digital Audio Player with Speaker (White)

text_fidelity_a:
Stellar Labs,Outdoor FM Antenna OMNIDIRECTIONAL 9/12/2015
Final Review:
Have now completed the installation and hookup of this antenna. The first test was to listen to Mixed Bag, 90.7 FM which was always full of static. Now this station comes in crystal clear, loud, and strong. Note that I decided to mount this antenna on the side of my house, just beneath the peak of my low roof facing the back yard. I had a quantity of twin 300 ohm cable which I wanted to use. Using a 300ohm/75ohm converter, I simply attached the end of the cable to the two 300ohm screws, protecting the connection with electrical tape. I measured and fabricated a wood mounting plate (see photo) and then screwed the mast bracket to it from the back. The wooden support board was then lag screwed, in turn, to the outside of my house just below the peak using 5" long screws. I then installed the antenna and mast, after reversing it. It now extends upwards vertically yet does not interfere with the roof line. The versatility of the mast permitted me to accomplish that.

(This review is preliminary. I assembled the antenna but am not yet ready to install it.
Assembly tips:

- Both curved antenna segments are secured to the antenna cross bar with the supplied hardware.
- The ends of one (bottom) segment are held in place with two phillips head screws. First, remove the curved metal clamp. line up the holes in the segment and, maintaining hand pressure on each segment end to ensure that it is seated firmly into it's curved metal seat, insert each screw and secure. Do not over tighten these fasteners. This is the "bottom" of the antenna, opposite the 75 ohm connector side. Attach one leg of the segment at a time.
- The ends of the second (top) segment are held in place with two hex head nuts. You will note that each nut is topped with a rubber 'O' ring. This is used to keep the nuts from threading off until assembly. Do not attempt to re-use these as they are not spacers or washers.
- Again, seat the ends of the antenna segment firmly in place, aligning the holes over the studs. Holding down the segment, install each nut. Do not over tighten these nuts.
- The closed loop ends of each antenna segment may now be gently guided in front of the black plastic locking clips. Once the looped ends are in position, firmly, yet carefully snap them into place. The circular antenna shape has now been completed. If assembled patiently and slowly, damage should not occur to the antenna.)
text_fidelity_b: Stellar Labs,Outdoor FM Antenna OMNIDIRECTIONAL

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 360 3.5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Text-To-Speech (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I've had this Nuvi 360 since Dec, 2006. It really works well. I carried it with me to DC. Even on foot it was terrific. It knew where all the restaurants and points of interest were and faithfully navigated us around the ancient horse paths of the Virginia/DC area. Believe me, when you pop out of an underground Metro station in the middle of the night and have no idea where you are or which direction to head off in, the ol' Garmin was there.

It's so small it easily fits in a pocket. The built-in battery lasts reasonably long. In the car, the 12-Volt adapter allows the unit to stay on indefinitely. You can select which accent and which gender you want the voice prompts to speak. Australian "Bruce," American "Jill" and a host of other combinations. All very fun. The voice prompts are the best. You really don't need to look at the thing while driving because it's uncanny in telling you what to do when you need to do it. It is amazingly accurate: something like 20 feet. It takes you right to the destination driveway.

It acquires the sats quickly and doesn't get flustered if you violate its recommendation and go in a different route. It just says, "recalculating" and finds another route for you. None of this "make a U-turn, bonehead!" It gives you enough time to make the turns, too. Also, it displays how far it is until the next turn. Very nice. No need to worry if you've missed it.

If you are planning on going to Europe, buy the unit that comes preloaded with both US and Europe maps as purchasing the Europe maps after the fact will really jump the cost unnecessarily.

I haven't used the Bluetooth capability yet but might later...after I get a Bluetooth phone.

The display is quite viewable in daylight and very bright at night, though it can be set to auto-dim at sundown so it's not too bright at night. You can touch the screen and scroll the map under your finger much like Google Maps can, to preview your route if desired. It shows coordinates and you can save them as destinations if desired, even if the location doesn't have an official street address. It is an MP3 player and can display photos and play Audible books on tape. When you are using the MP3 or Audible features, it pauses the file playing back to announce directions, then returns to the file without losing any of the MP3 file or book info. Very nice.

At extra cost, it has the ability to add foreign language dictionaries which can verbally speak phrases and words to you. You can also add Travel Guides and other software via the SD chip slot.

Overall, I'm very pleased with this device. It's accurate, fast, functional and small.

The one thing that doesn't work is the windshield suction mount. It broke before I even used it once. The plastic loops on the suction cup that receive the ball arm's hinge pin are too thin and fragile and broke with just a little normal hinge adjustment.

I recommend the model 010-10908-00 friction mount that looks like a bean bag with a ball arm sticking up. I made something similar by taking an unneeded 1/4" thick mousepad and epoxying a couple of small 1" x 1" angle brackets to the pad to hold the ball arm that I salvaged from the broken suction cup mount.

A friction mount is interchangeable with multiple vehicles, doesn't slide around on the dash and allows complete and rapid removal and/or hiding to avoid theft. Plus, you don't have to glue a disk to the dash for the suction cup to attach to.

UPDATE 10-22-07:
The 360 works well enough; better than most. It should: Five point three bills should deliver one heck of a map!

I've had it since Dec 2006...less than one year. Today I get an offer from Garmin to update my North American map software for a mere point seven bills. That's AFTER the five point three bills I already sunk into this little electronic gizmo.

I heard Garmin has a one year free map update policy, but their website won't let me do it. Not cool. The cost of the unit has already fallen significantly from what I originally paid and now they want more to get it current, within a year of purchase. Not cool at all. Also, impossible to contact by email. Garmin website is in a permanent loop back to itself when clicking on the "contact by email" option. Otherwise, it's call and wait on hold between certain times. Not cool again.

Then a friend says how well his Verizon GPS works on his wireless phone. I look into that. Verizon offers a full time GPS cost and a single use option for under three bucks per use.

For what I have wasted on this Garmin--over five bills and counting upward forever with their unfriendly updates--that's a whole heck of a lot of one-time Verizon uses with what will be the most updated, most accurate database. After all, no one's going to beat the phone company with accurate phone numbers and addresses.

If I hadn't already bought into the Garmin ripoff, I'd definitely go with Verizon's phone based GPS: the phone will always be with you when you need it instead of in the glove compartment in the other car.

And it most likely won't get stolen. It's a darned pain to have to put the Garmin away after each use so some cretin won't bash in a window to steal a very, very expensive toy that could just as easily fit inside a phone.

Go with the phone.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 360 3.5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Text-To-Speech (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Mohu Television Antenna Leaf 30 Paper-Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna for Free TV MH-110502 There are so many good reviews here about this antenna, I'll try not to repeat what others have said. I do have a few tips to add,

When setting up your antenna, do yourself a favor and tie a string through the two holes at the top of the antenna. That way you can hang it on one tack/nail as you're searching for the best location. Have extra tacks or nails handy, as they will jump out of your hand and become lost in the carpet (until you find them the next day with a bare foot).

Buy some very small nails. I've discovered that I need to move the antenna around to get reception for some channels. Therefore I have a fair number of nails in the wall that look a little strange. Small nails are less visually distracting. If I get very ambitious, I might even paint them.

This antenna really works best on an exterior wall facing the majority of transmitting antennas you are trying to reach. So if you're working with an interior wall facing the wrong direction, it probably won't work very well.

To up the number of channels you receive, consider buying a signal amplifier (I bought the RCA Digital Amplifier here on Amazon.) They cost about $15. I added 10 additional channels by using one.

Finally, how well these indoor antennas work largely depends on where you live and how close you are to the transmitting antennas. To avoid disappointment, do some research online before purchasing anything.The site that helped me the most was disablemycable.com .
text_fidelity_b: Mohu Television Antenna Leaf 30 Paper-Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna for Free TV MH-110502

text_fidelity_a:
Mokata Headphone Bluetooth Wireless Over Ear On Foldable Hi-fi Stereo Headset with AUX 3.5mm Jack Cord SD Card Slot Microphone for Young Adults Cellphone TV Rechargeable Equipment B02 Red I got this set of headphones to go with our panasonic phone system in your house for our landline. Many times we get power failures so we still keep a landline. But when the power is not out, I like to use our landline for calls. Our system uses bluetooth for headsets so this is where these came in handy.

HOW ARE THESE?
These headphones are red. I love the color. they seem sturdier than expected, There is a slot in the headphones which you can insert a MicroSD card so you don't HAVE to use a player with the headphones (like phone or MP3, etc). These are bluetooth as well and have a volume button.

HOW DO THESE PERFORM?
My family is a bunch of ear phone addicted fanatics. We have some of the best and some of the worst and everything in between. When I started to try these out, I really liked them and was surprised at how loud they were. One of our kids, a daughter, grabbed the headphones to try them and loved them so much, she is getting a pair for her pottery studio to listen to her own music.

ARE THEY TOO LOUD?
I did not think these were too loud. They were controlled easily through the volume control on the headphones.

ARE THEY COMFORTABLE?
I use these mainly to talk on the phone so I don't have to cradle the phone to my head when working while talking. These are comfortable and as long as I am not SUPER active with these on, they seem to stay on fairly well. They are comfortable and my ears last about a half hour before I want to remove them. Sometimes longer.

CHARGING
These do not take long at all to charge. Within a few hours they were ready to go.

ADJUSTABLE?
These are not hard to adjust and they seem to adapt well to all of our heads.

SOUND QUALITY
The sound quality is surprisingly good with these. There is good definition and it is not muffled or out of proportion to the point that you prefer them not to be on. Let me just say that the daughter that is going to buy these is so impressed she is very excited for this price to get her own pair. She is very picky about her ear buds or headphones.

DO THEY BLOCK NOISE?
These do block outside noise well which is another great feature of these.

VOICE?
So far the voice works well with these when I use them on the phone.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a decent set of headphones that are comfortable, block outside noise well, and do well on the phone for both listening and voice as well as music, these are a great choice. I love the red color too.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. These are great, affordable and work well so far. I will update if anything changes.

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 42LM 4.3-Inch Portable Vehicle GPS with Lifetime Maps (US) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I bought this trusting the good reviews. I live in an area undergoing major road construction on all the highways, and I wanted the GPS to help me route around it when I run errands and go to appointments. I figured the "lifetime map updates" feature would ensure this GPS shows the latest road closures to get me through the city without trouble. WRONG.

Not only does it NOT show the ongoing road construction they started months ago near my house, but it has tried to send me off an exit on another highway that has been closed for 2+ years! And when I couldn't take that exit, it refused to reroute, and kept trying to get me to take the next exit to turn around and then sent me BACK to the long-closed exit. Almost NONE of the road closures are on the GPS map, and it will not reroute even when I hit the reroute button. It is very frustrating.

We have taken the latest map updates, and even contacted Garmin, whose response was that they were sorry they had a backlog of "a lot of updates" and they were "trying to put them in as quickly as possible" -- but sending me to an exit that's been closed over 2 years says otherwise. I HATE this GPS. I only gave it 2 stars because I like the graphics options and it lets you take screen shots of the map. If it WORKED properly, I'd say it could have been a great GPS, but it doesn't do what it promised.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 42LM 4.3-Inch Portable Vehicle GPS with Lifetime Maps (US) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech NEW Logitech Webcam C210 (Cameras & Frames) I received the Logitech VideoCam and was surprised at one, how easy and quick the setup took; second, I was amazed at the quality of the picture. This is my first time at WebCam and was apprehensive at the standard of quality. But in 1,2,3 steps it was up. The voices are clear and it depends whether you use Logitech viewing or Skype, but Logitech has a more refined lip movement to voice coordination. Again...this is a perfect picture!

Surprisingly, the 3MP photo option is quite impressive. I love the shoot picture instantly. You can quickly add a friend to chat with, just enter their email address. Either at your end of the recipients end you can quickly snap a picture and that pic can be the photo of choice for the friend or family. It is easy to have several different pictures on the interface of the Webcam; I dragged a few from the desktop. My webcam sits comfortably on top of the computer. If I need to remove the camera from the top of computer to show a different view of my background, or reveal other parts of the house, I can do that easily with the 5-feet long attached cord, although it could be longer.

You can make several adjustments, and the light adjustment is automatic, the mic is noise cancelling, however, I have not the need to test that yet.

What I like is that anytime someone on your contact list is at the computer, you can have a small message pop up that lets you know they are available. My two current contacts are using Windows XP; while I am on Windows Vista.

If you are someone you know is vascillating between getting a Webcam, I encourage them to do so, especially if they have family miles away like I do. Many people do not like to be on camera, and for me, I don't either because I have to look decent an any moment a call comes in. Try it.... You may like it! ....Rizzo
text_fidelity_b: Logitech NEW Logitech Webcam C210 (Cameras & Frames)

text_fidelity_a:
TomTom XL 350 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator The good:

Lane guidance. I like to plan my turns and exits, especially in thick traffic. I hate it when the passenger who claims to know the way suddenly says "Left turn here!" to feet from the intersection when I'm in the right lane and the middle and left lanes are packed with traffic. No more. Tom Tom says things like, "Take a right on 17th street, then a left on Maritime Road, giving me time to get into that left lane." It also gives you lane guidance for exiting the highway, when it's right two lanes for this highway, and middle two for this bridge and left one for the other bridge. You can see on screen, and it tells you aloud, which land you want.

It tells you "left turn here", which is good when the street sign is missing or obscured.

It adapts quickly. It seems to know traffic laws, so it doesn't try to put you the wrong way on a one way the way Mapquest did in the early days.

It tracks your speed.

The route chosen to a familiar location surprised me, but thinking it over, it was the most direct route. I normal go one exit on the highway. It had me go a few very small side streets instead.

It works in or out of the car, for those who want to use it for camping or geocaching.

The bad:

Even on the loudest setting, it's a little hard to hear. The pronunciation is off, which one might expect, but the volume is poor. It's hard to hear, even with no one talking in the car. Good luck if you've got kids in the back seat.

It was a little hard to figure out. It wants the street then the number, and I tried offering the full address. Once I figured it out, it was pretty easy and did a great job.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom XL 350 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator

This caused a lot of problems and I was constantly transferring my images to an external HDD and it was extremely inconvenient.

I decided to purchase this USB flash drive. It was low cost for such a large amount of space. Best decision I ever made!
I have had this in my laptop for the last 2 months and it has not fallen out or gotten damaged. I carry my laptop everywhere with me.
Data transfers are very fast. With less than 50 picutures, it's basically instant and I often feel the need to check and make sure the files actually transferred because it happens so quickly, I don't even get a "Transferring files" window. I have never had a failed transfer.

If you are using it in a mac, you will need to reformat it to ExFAT. It will work out of the box, but will not accept large folders or files until it is reformatted.

The only issue I've ever had is if my computer falls asleep, the drive will sometimes disconnect, but that is due to the settings on my computer and not the drive. A simple unplug-replug reconnects it.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk Ultra Fit 16GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive SDCZ43-016G-G46

text_fidelity_a:
PreSonus C3.5 BT Channel Studio Monitor I have been wanting to get a bluetooth speaker for connecting to my tablet for a while so I was very pleased to get an opportunity to try this speaker set. It is far and away better than what I originally had in mind and so far I am more than pleased with them.

Setup of these speakers is straightforward and simple, so much so that instructions really are not needed to get started. The wire connector is color-coded to make connecting the speakers to each other almost completely foolproof. If I have any complaints about the setup it would be that the wire connector is a little on the short side but that’s an easy fix - just buy longer wire.

I enabled bluetooth on my tablet, told the speaker set to make itself available and the tablet connected to it immediately. One could not ask for anything simpler. The process took less than a minute and most of that time was spent walking across the room to press the bluetooth button on the speakers.

I loaded up Pandora and told the tablet to play and almost immediately it was clear that these speakers are far above average. The sound profile is stunning - clear and crisp highs, rich midrange and very satisfying bass without overdriving. These speakers do an outstanding job of accurately reproducing the sound. On the back of the main (control) speaker there are two knobs for adjusting the highs and lows should the middle be unsatisfactory for some reason. These speakers also do a good job with spacial elements and there is depth to the sound.

I paired the speakers with my laptop (once I powered off the tablet) as well and it was also very easy.

I took some cables and wired the speakers to an older television in the house to see how much better watching TV would be. It was definitely better and it have a more spacial and stereo sound experience but with our TV this prevented us from making any volume adjustments unless we turned the volume knob on the speaker itself. This is a minor nuisance but certainly not a real issue.

In addition to great sound, these seem to be well-build and rugged, a good sign right out of the box. These are an excellent choice for a home theater system or an audiophile's listening room.

So far I have found nothing about which to complain with these speakers. Set-up is a snap and the sound quality is just amazing. These are speakers for the serious listener.
text_fidelity_b: PreSonus C3.5 BT Channel Studio Monitor
